questions.question:
**Direction: Select the grammatically correct sentence.**

A. Today is sixth day of our workshop. All the participants are highly enthusiastic.

B. Today is a sixth day of our workshop. All the participants are highly enthusiastic.

C. Today is the sixth day of our workshop. All the participants are highly enthusiastic.

D. Today is sixth day of our workshop. All participants are highly enthusiastic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is *"Today is the sixth day of our workshop. All the participants are highly enthusiastic."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We use the definite article **"the"** with ordinal numbers **(first, second, third, etc.) **and sequence words (such as next and last) that precede a noun.

 
 
• Example: *This is **the third**__ time you have been late.*
 
 
 
• The word** "sixth" **is an ordinal number, so we must use **"the" **before it.
 
• The phrase **"all the participants"** is either neutral in stress, or slightly emphasizes **"participants."**
 
• So,** "All the participants"** is the correct phrase to use instead of **"all participants."**
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct with proper capitalization and punctuation.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

Was the conference not attended by them?

options.text: Did they not attend the conference?
Does they not attend the conference?
Do they not attend the conference?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Did they not attend the conference?"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Passive Voice. It is in Simple Past Tense(Interrogative, Negative sentence ).
 
• As per the given question, we must change it to Active Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Did + Subject + not+ V1 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Was/were + Subject (objective case) + not + V3 + by + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Did they not solve the question? (Active Voice)*
 
• *Was the question not solved by them? (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'they'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'the conference'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• The preposition 'by' will be removed. 
 
• In this sentence,** "they" **is the subject and **"attend"** is the action, so we can make it active by putting **"they" **before** "attend" **to get "**Did they not attend the conference?"**
 
• The correct answer is option 1.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.**

Neither John nor Simon **__are coming to the meeting__**.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"is coming to the meeting."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"Neither John nor Simon"**, which is a compound subject.
 
• When **"neither ...... nor"** links singular terms, the verb is singular.
 
• When the subjects are connected by **"nor",** the verb should agree with the subject closest to it.
 
 
• **Example: ***Neither the car nor the truck is available.*
 
 
 
• In this case, it is **"Simon."**
 
• **"Is coming" **is the correct verb form for the singular subject **"Simon".**
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

 

**Correct sentence:** *Neither John nor Simon **is coming to the meeting**__.*

The family is neither interested in selling the house **__or rebuilding__** it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"nor rebuilding."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The use of **"neither"** at the beginning of the sentence requires the use of a negative conjunction.
 
• The sentence requires a negative conjunction to show that the family is not interested in both selling and rebuilding the house.
 
• We use **neither … nor** when we are talking about two or more things that are not true or that do not happen. 
 
• **"Nor"** is a negative conjunction that connects two negative clauses.
 
• The sentence would be grammatically incorrect if** "or" **was used instead of **"nor."**
 
 
• **Example:** *The play was **neither as funny nor as exciting**__ as she said it was.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

**Correct sentence:** *The family is neither interested in selling the house __**nor rebuilding**__ it.*
